messages:
tian: Heads up — canary rollout is on hold. Seeing ~30% token/sec drop in continuous-batcher after merge rfc/queue-prefetch-8452. Initial flame shows kernel selection falling back to generic memcpy on drain path for small batches. Need triage and a quick mitigation :eyes:

nora: Ugh. Which metric exactly? token/sec across cluster or just canary shards?

tian: token/sec averaged across the canary shards. Per-shard graphs: http://grafana/redwood/ctb-tokensec?canary=42 (short link)

kevin: perf-ci reported a regression too?

perf-ci: CI perf check failed on 8452: benchmark/ctb_throughput_small_batches dropped 28% vs baseline. Artifacts: https://ci/redwood/8452/artifacts/perf.tar.gz

maria: Also seeing KV cache hit-rate dip ~12% for the same windows. Might be related: if kernel choice increases memcopy time, drain latency grows -> prefetch window misfires -> lower kvcache reuse.

sam: 8452 changed the kernel policy heuristics to prefer the new "unified-copy" path when batch_size >= 8, but there was a subtle off-by-one in effective batch_count estimate. Small batches (4-7) are now taking the generic path. I flagged it in review but it got merged with perf tests passing locally.

tian: Posting the hot profile snippet from a canary GPU (stripped):
```
# top 5 kernels by time
memcpy_generic  62.3%
unified_copy   12.1%
attention_fused 8.9%
kv_prefetch     7.2%
other           9.5%
```
This is for sequences ~64, batch_size ~5. Previously memcpy_generic was <20% for same config.

kevin: Sounds like the selection threshold logic calc_batch_count() got bumped. Can we bisect to the merge commit and revert candidate?

sam: I ran a quick git bisect locally across the PR series. Culprit is commit c3f9b7a (policy: use unified when est_batch >= 8 -> bug in est_batch when coalescing).

nora: We should either revert that commit or ship a targeted hotfix that forces the old policy for small-batch drains. Which is faster?

maria: Hotfix seems safer — revert touches other unrelated perf fixes in the same PR. Quick patch: clamp est_batch to floor(derived/2) for the decision path. I can draft.

sam: Alternatively, short-term override config: set KERNEL_POLICY_OVERRIDE=prefer_old_for_small_batches for rollout groups. That avoids code churn.

tian: Can we test the override? I'll apply env override on canary and run the perf job.

# command
```
kubectl set env deploy/ctb-canary KERNEL_POLICY_OVERRIDE=prefer_old_for_small_batches -n prod-canaries
./ci/run_bench --target canary --bench ctb_throughput_small_batches
```

tian: Test result: token/sec recovered to within 3% of baseline, KV hit-rate back up +10%. Uploading logs: https://ci/redwood/quicktest/3176543210/logs

deploy-bot: Rollout hold lifted for canary group 42 (manual override applied).

kevin: Great. Next steps: open a small PR to fix est_batch calc and add a unit test + perf guard. Also add a config flag to flip policy per-deployment so we can roll forward safely.

maria: I'll open PR #3857 with the clamp + test. Includes microbench for batch sizes 1..12.

nora: Add a release note and mark the original change for follow-up in postmortem. We need an eval to detect this class earlier: detect when memcpy_generic dominates >40% for small batches.

sam: Adding a CI perf alert for ctb_throughput_small_batches with finer granularity (fail if regression >10% on small batch subset).

tian: Once #3857 passes CI, let's remove KERNEL_POLICY_OVERRIDE from canary and re-run canary to confirm stable.

maria: PR landed and CI is green on the clamp. Can someone approve the rollback policy removal?

kevin: Approving. Will watch metrics during promote.

deploy-bot: KERNEL_POLICY_OVERRIDE removed from canary 42. Promote scheduled to prod-canaries in 5m.

tian: Post-promo checks: token/sec steady, KV hit-rate normalized, no downstream latency spikes. Canary looks healthy :thumbsup:

nora: Nice work. Please add the perf traces and the bisect note to the postmortem folder (incidents/). Also tag the PRs and include the perf artifacts.

sam: Filed perf CI tweak: https://ci/redwood/alerts/ctb_small_batch.json.

kevin: Closing the rollout blocker. If we see recurrence, we should consider a short-lived canary gate requiring the small-batch perf check to pass before auto-promote.

maria: Agreed. I'll draft the gate proposal.
